# Plan A: Release Binaries — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Set up the GitHub Releases pipeline so that pushing `v0.1.0` produces prebuilt `tplot` binaries for macOS arm64, macOS x86_64, and Linux x86_64 (gnu), plus an auto-generated `tplot-installer.sh` for one-line install via curl. A separate CI workflow runs test/clippy/fmt on every push and PR.

**Architecture:** `cargo-dist` (axodotdev/cargo-dist) generates the release pipeline. Config in `dist-workspace.toml` at repo root. Hand-written `ci.yml` is independent. CHANGELOG.md drives release notes. The first release is `v0.1.0`.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 2024 (workspace), GitHub Actions, cargo-dist, Keep-a-Changelog, MIT OR Apache-2.0 license.

**Inherited context (Plans 1–13.6):**
- 16 chart types working; 348 tests passing.
- Workspace at `version = "0.1.0"`, `repository = "https://github.com/TomekNocon/tplot"`.
- Branches `main` and `feature/foundation` already pushed to `git@github.com:TomekNocon/tplot.git` (the remote is live).
- Email attribution: `tomek.lm10@gmail.com` for every commit.

## Task 1: Add workspace and crate metadata

**Files:**
- Modify: `Cargo.toml`
- Modify: `crates/tplot/Cargo.toml`

cargo-dist and crates.io both want descriptive metadata. We add it now so cargo-dist's installer messaging is accurate and so future Plan C (cargo publish) is unblocked.

- [ ] **Step 1: Extend `[workspace.package]` in `Cargo.toml`**

Replace lines 11–15 of `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[workspace.package]
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
repository = "https://github.com/TomekNocon/tplot"
```

with:

```toml
[workspace.package]
version     = "0.1.0"
edition     = "2024"
license     = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
repository  = "https://github.com/TomekNocon/tplot"
homepage    = "https://github.com/TomekNocon/tplot"
description = "Storytelling-first terminal data visualization."
readme      = "README.md"
keywords    = ["chart", "plot", "cli", "terminal", "data"]
categories  = ["command-line-utilities", "visualization"]
authors     = ["Tomek Nocon <tomek.lm10@gmail.com>"]
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Make `crates/tplot/Cargo.toml` inherit the new fields**

Edit the `[package]` block (currently lines 1–6). Replace:

```toml
[package]
name = "tplot"
version.workspace      = true
edition.workspace      = true
license.workspace      = true
repository.workspace   = true
```

with:

```toml
[package]
name = "tplot"
version.workspace      = true
edition.workspace      = true
license.workspace      = true
repository.workspace   = true
homepage.workspace     = true
description.workspace  = true
readme.workspace       = true
keywords.workspace     = true
categories.workspace   = true
authors.workspace      = true
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Verify metadata propagates**

Run:

```bash
cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json; p=[x for x in json.load(sys.stdin)['packages'] if x['name']=='tplot'][0]; print('description:', p['description']); print('homepage:', p['homepage']); print('keywords:', p['keywords']); print('categories:', p['categories'])"
```

Expected output:
```
description: Storytelling-first terminal data visualization.
homepage: https://github.com/TomekNocon/tplot
keywords: ['chart', 'plot', 'cli', 'terminal', 'data']
categories: ['command-line-utilities', 'visualization']
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Build sanity check**

Run: `cargo check --workspace`
Expected: `Finished` with no errors.

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add Cargo.toml crates/tplot/Cargo.toml
git commit -m "Add workspace and crate metadata (description, keywords, categories)"
```

## Task 2: Add license files

**Files:**
- Create: `LICENSE-MIT`
- Create: `LICENSE-APACHE`

The workspace declares `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"` but ships no license files. cargo-dist's installer doesn't require them, but every dual-licensed Rust crate has both files at the root, and Plan C (`cargo publish`) will hard-fail without them.

- [ ] **Step 1: Create `LICENSE-MIT`**

Write to `LICENSE-MIT`:

```
MIT License

Copyright (c) 2026 Tomek Nocon

Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy
of this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal
in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights
to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell
copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is
furnished to do so, subject to the following conditions:

The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all
copies or substantial portions of the Software.

THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR
IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY,
FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE
AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER
LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM,
OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE
SOFTWARE.
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Fetch the canonical Apache 2.0 text**

Apache License 2.0 is ~200 lines of unchanging boilerplate; we fetch it from the Apache Software Foundation's official URL and verify integrity rather than embedding it inline.

```bash
curl -sSfL https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt -o LICENSE-APACHE
shasum -a 256 LICENSE-APACHE
```

Expected SHA256: `cfc7749b96f63bd31c3c42b5c471bf756814053e847c10f3eb003417bc523d30`

(This hash was captured from the canonical Apache Software Foundation URL on 2026-05-01. If the SHA differs, the file was corrupted in transit OR the ASF updated the document — re-run the curl, and if the SHA is still different, manually verify the new content matches Apache 2.0 before committing. Do **not** edit the file manually otherwise.)

- [ ] **Step 3: Spot-check the file**

Run:
```bash
head -3 LICENSE-APACHE
wc -l LICENSE-APACHE
```

Expected:
```
                                 Apache License
                           Version 2.0, January 2004
                        http://www.apache.org/licenses/
202
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Commit**

```bash
git add LICENSE-MIT LICENSE-APACHE
git commit -m "Add LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE (dual MIT/Apache-2.0 license)"
```

## Task 3: Add CHANGELOG.md

**Files:**
- Create: `CHANGELOG.md`

cargo-dist auto-pulls the matching `## [version]` section into release notes. Initial entry summarizes everything shipped to date.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write `CHANGELOG.md`**

```markdown
# Changelog

All notable changes to `tplot` are documented here.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
While < 1.0.0, the CLI surface (flag names, output format) may change between
minor versions.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.1.0] - 2026-05-01

### Added

- 16 chart types covering common analysis needs:
  bar, hist, line, scatter, sparkline, heatmap, box, area, candlestick,
  treemap, violin, ridgeline, sankey, table, summary.
- Storytelling layer: focal/context palette (burnt orange focal, gray
  context), trust-score gate (max ≥ 1.5× median), and embedded one-line
  takeaway. `--neutral`, `--focus`, `--annotate`, `--no-takeaway` flags
  for fine control.
- Hybrid renderers — half-blocks (`▀▄█`), vertical-blocks (`▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█`),
  and Braille (2×4 dots) — auto-selected based on chart type.
- Image protocols: Kitty graphics protocol, iTerm2 inline-image (OSC 1337),
  auto-detected via OSC capability probing with timeouts.
- Theme detection (light/dark) via `$COLORFGBG` and `$TERM_PROGRAM`.
- Single-line `tplot summary` chart, designed for inline rendering in
  Claude Code where multi-line output is collapsed behind Ctrl+O.
- JSON ChartSpec dispatch via `tplot json` for programmatic input.
- Per-renderer ANSI escape compaction (3.2-13.6× byte reduction in tests).
- Three palettes: `signature`, `editorial`, `colorblind-safe`.
- 348 tests across the 5-crate workspace.

[Unreleased]: https://github.com/TomekNocon/tplot/compare/v0.1.0...HEAD
[0.1.0]: https://github.com/TomekNocon/tplot/releases/tag/v0.1.0
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Verify markdown renders**

Run: `head -10 CHANGELOG.md && grep -c "^##" CHANGELOG.md`

Expected: file starts with `# Changelog` heading; `grep -c` reports `2` (one for `[Unreleased]`, one for `[0.1.0]`).

- [ ] **Step 3: Commit**

```bash
git add CHANGELOG.md
git commit -m "Add CHANGELOG.md (initial 0.1.0 entry)"
```

## Task 4: Install cargo-dist and run init

**Files:**
- Create: `dist-workspace.toml` (generated)
- Create: `.github/workflows/release.yml` (generated)

`cargo-dist` is interactive. We accept its defaults except where called out below.

- [ ] **Step 1: Install cargo-dist**

```bash
cargo install cargo-dist --locked
cargo dist --version
```

Expected: prints a version string (e.g. `cargo-dist 0.x.y` or `dist 0.x.y`). If the binary is named `dist` rather than `cargo-dist`, substitute `dist` for `cargo dist` in subsequent steps.

- [ ] **Step 2: Run `cargo dist init`**

```bash
cargo dist init
```

Wizard answers:

| Prompt | Answer |
|---|---|
| Hosting platform | GitHub Releases |
| Build / publish CI | GitHub Actions |
| Targets | check `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` (uncheck everything else) |
| Installers | check `shell` (uncheck `powershell`, `homebrew`, `npm`, etc) |
| Pre-release versions in PRs (`pr-run-mode`) | `plan` (the default — runs sanity checks on PRs without producing artifacts) |
| Auto-include README, CHANGELOG, LICENSE in archives | yes |
| Use `cargo install` as a fallback installer | optional, defer to default (usually no) |
| Anything else | accept defaults |

- [ ] **Step 3: Inspect the generated `dist-workspace.toml`**

Run: `cat dist-workspace.toml`

Verify it contains (modulo formatting / version of cargo-dist):
- A `targets = [...]` array with exactly the 3 triples above
- An `installers = ["shell"]` (or equivalent) entry
- A `dist-version` matching the installed cargo-dist version

If any of those differ, edit the file directly to match — cargo-dist is happy to consume hand-edited config.

- [ ] **Step 4: Inspect `.github/workflows/release.yml`**

Run: `grep -E "(workflow_dispatch|tags|matrix:|aarch64|x86_64)" .github/workflows/release.yml`

Verify:
- `workflow_dispatch:` trigger present (default; needed for the dry-run in Task 7)
- `tags:` trigger present (default)
- All 3 target triples appear in the build matrix

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add dist-workspace.toml .github/workflows/release.yml Cargo.toml
git commit -m "Add cargo-dist release pipeline (3 targets, shell installer)"
```

`Cargo.toml` is included because cargo-dist's init usually adds a `[workspace.metadata.dist]` block or bumps `[profile.dist]`. If `git status` shows it unchanged, drop it from the `git add`.

## Task 5: Add CI workflow

**Files:**
- Create: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

Independent of the release pipeline. Runs on every push to `main` and every PR.

- [ ] **Step 1: Create the workflow**

Write to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    name: test + lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy, rustfmt
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: cargo test
        run: cargo test --workspace --all-targets
      - name: cargo clippy
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - name: cargo fmt
        run: cargo fmt --all --check
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Lint the YAML locally**

Run: `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'))" && echo OK`

Expected: `OK`. If yaml.safe_load throws, fix the syntax.

- [ ] **Step 3: Commit**

```bash
git add .github/workflows/ci.yml
git commit -m "Add CI workflow (test, clippy, fmt) for push to main and PRs"
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Edit README.md**

Replace the existing `## Install` block (currently 4 lines: heading + a `cargo install --path` snippet) with:

```markdown
## Install

### One-liner (recommended)

```bash
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf \
  https://github.com/TomekNocon/tplot/releases/latest/download/tplot-installer.sh | sh
```

This grabs the right prebuilt binary for your platform, drops it on your `PATH`, and is what most users want.

### Manual download

Pick the archive matching your platform from the [latest release](https://github.com/TomekNocon/tplot/releases/latest):

| Platform | Archive |
|---|---|
| macOS, Apple silicon | `tplot-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.xz` |
| macOS, Intel         | `tplot-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.xz` |
| Linux, x86_64 (gnu)  | `tplot-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz` |

```bash
curl -L https://github.com/TomekNocon/tplot/releases/latest/download/tplot-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.xz \
  | tar xJ
sudo mv tplot /usr/local/bin/
```

Verify checksums against `SHA256SUMS` published with each release.

### From source

```bash
cargo install --path crates/tplot
```
```

## Task 7: Local dry-run with `cargo dist build`

`cargo dist build` runs the packaging logic locally for the host target only. It's a fast pre-flight before the GitHub Actions matrix.

- [ ] **Step 1: Run the local build**

```bash
cargo dist build
```

Expected: succeeds, prints lines like `Built tplot-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.xz` (or whatever your host target is).

- [ ] **Step 2: Inspect the archive**

```bash
ls -la target/distrib/
tar -tJf target/distrib/tplot-*.tar.xz | head
```

Expected: an archive containing at minimum `tplot/tplot` (the binary), `tplot/README.md`, `tplot/LICENSE-MIT`, `tplot/LICENSE-APACHE`, `tplot/CHANGELOG.md`. Cargo-dist's exact layout differs slightly between versions; the binary is the only required entry.

- [ ] **Step 3: Smoke-test the binary**

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/tplot-dryrun && cd /tmp/tplot-dryrun
tar xJf "$OLDPWD/target/distrib/"tplot-*.tar.xz
./tplot/tplot --version
./tplot/tplot summary - -y v <<<$'v\n10\n20\n30\n40\n50'
cd "$OLDPWD"
```

Expected: `--version` prints `tplot 0.1.0`. `summary` prints exactly one line.

- [ ] **Step 4: No commit needed.** This task validates without producing repo changes. (`target/distrib/` is git-ignored.)

## Task 8: Push the branch and cut the first release

**This task is operator-driven** — it requires user actions in the GitHub UI and on the user's machine. The plan documents the sequence; subagents should not push tags on the user's behalf.

- [ ] **Step 1: Push the feature branch**

```bash
git push origin feature/foundation
```

Expected: pushes the new commits from Tasks 1-6.

- [ ] **Step 2: Trigger a `workflow_dispatch` dry run**

Open `https://github.com/TomekNocon/tplot/actions` → pick the `Release` workflow → click `Run workflow` → choose branch `feature/foundation` → run.

Expected: a dry-run that builds all 3 archives but does NOT publish to a GitHub Release (cargo-dist's default behavior for `workflow_dispatch` without an explicit version input). Verify all 3 matrix legs go green.

If a leg fails: read the log, fix the underlying issue, push, re-run dispatch. Do not cut the real tag yet.

- [ ] **Step 3: Merge to main**

Once dispatch goes green, open a PR and merge `feature/foundation → main` (or fast-forward locally and push). The CI workflow runs on the merge; verify it goes green.

- [ ] **Step 4: Cut the real release**

```bash
git checkout main
git pull
git tag v0.1.0
git push origin v0.1.0
```

Expected: the tag push triggers `release.yml`. Watch the run at `https://github.com/TomekNocon/tplot/actions`.

- [ ] **Step 5: Verify the release**

Open `https://github.com/TomekNocon/tplot/releases/v0.1.0`.

Expected assets:
- `tplot-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.xz`
- `tplot-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.xz`
- `tplot-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz`
- `tplot-installer.sh`
- `SHA256SUMS` (or `*.sha256` files alongside each archive — cargo-dist version-dependent)

Release notes should match the `## [0.1.0]` section of `CHANGELOG.md`.

- [ ] **Step 6: Smoke-test the public installer**

On a fresh shell (or a different machine):

```bash
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf \
  https://github.com/TomekNocon/tplot/releases/latest/download/tplot-installer.sh | sh
tplot --version
```

Expected: `tplot 0.1.0`.

If everything works, the plan is done.

## Failure-Mode Reference

| What broke | First check |
|---|---|
| `cargo metadata` doesn't show new fields after Task 1 | typo in `[workspace.package]` keys; verify with `cargo metadata --no-deps` |
| Apache 2.0 SHA mismatch | network corruption; re-run curl. Don't hand-edit the file. |
| `cargo dist init` doesn't include `workflow_dispatch` | edit `.github/workflows/release.yml` to add `workflow_dispatch: {}` under `on:` |
| Workflow dispatch run fails on macOS x86_64 | `macos-13` runner is being deprecated by GitHub eventually; check Actions logs and bump to a newer runner image in `release.yml` |
| Release notes are blank | CHANGELOG.md heading must be exactly `## [0.1.0]` with brackets — cargo-dist matches that format literally |
| Tag push doesn't trigger workflow | likely a typo in the tag (`v.0.1.0`, `0.1.0` without `v`, etc); delete tag, retag |
| Installer.sh fails on user's machine | mismatched architecture detection; report the user's `uname -ms` output |

- ✓ Type/name consistency: `tplot-installer.sh` referenced consistently; CHANGELOG headings match `[X.Y.Z]` format throughout.
- ✓ Operator-only steps (Task 8) clearly flagged so subagents don't accidentally push tags.
